title: dynamic-reservation-curves-and-enterprise-sq-scenarios
creator: Aisha Patel
summary: Design and run a set of experiments to validate three packaging options for Dedicated capacity: (1) flat reserved GPU tiers with ramped discounts, (2) hybrid reserved + burst credits curve that decays usage-based prices with committed GPU-months, and (3) autoscale-first offering with negotiated baseline and overage rules. Parallel work to update the enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) with Dedicated-specific artifacts (KMS, audit logs, network isolation, upgrade policy) and produce contract language templates for sales.
acceptance_criteria: Run three pricing experiments across 10 pilot customers and collect conversion and retention signals
Produce per-variant ARR and committed GPU-month forecasts with modeled unit economics
Converge on one recommended default packaging option and an alternate enterprise-only SKU
SQ updated with Dedicated-specific answers and artifacts; legal sign-off obtained
Sales enablement playbook and pricing calculator published in Confluence

tradeoffs_and_notes: Burst credits reduce friction for customers that spike but complicate billing reconciliation and SRE capacity planning.
Autoscale-first SKU reduces upfront commitment friction but lowers committed ARR predictability and may increase unit costs unless we enforce baseline reservation windows.
Flat reserved tiers are easiest for sales and contracts, but may deter customers with spiky workloads and can increase underutilization risk.
Operational cost visibility (per-GPU-month and per-token marginal cost) must be surfaced in console to prevent customer confusion.
Legal requested explicit upgrade/downgrade windows to avoid post-commit churn; this may require changes to the Dedicated billing pipeline.
experiment_design: Variant A - Flat Reserved: three tiers (S/M/L) with 10/20/30 GPU reserved bundles and stepped discounts at 6/12 month commits
Variant B - Hybrid Reserved+Burst: smaller reserved bundles + burst credits pool; price per burst token decays as committed GPU-months increase
Variant C - Autoscale Baseline+Overage: baseline reserved capacity with autoscale enabled; baseline priced at a premium and overage billed at on-demand rate with a cap
Success metrics: pilot conversion rate >= 20% of engaged accounts, committed GPU-months delta >= +25% vs baseline, churn rate <= 5% at 90 days, ARR delta modeled with 95% confidence interval
Telemetry plan: instrument signup funnel, long-lived commitment signing, token consumption by variant, and billing reconciliation failures
stakeholders: Engineering: Connor Lee (eng lead), Mei Chen (runtime), Lucas Park (billing)
decision_points: If Variant B yields >10% higher committed GPU-months than A with <10% added billing ops overhead, recommend B as default
If Variant C improves signups but reduces 12-month ARR forecast by >15%, surface as enterprise-only SKU behind sales approval
If SQ updates require >2 weeks of engineering artifacts changes (KMS/HSM integrations, audit log retention), then delay GA release and label as enterprise v1
